title: Variables and types
bridge: C has `int`, `double`, `char` and (with `<stdbool.h>`) `bool`. There's no string type: text is an array of `char` (coming in a later unit). Integer division drops the remainder: `7 / 2` is `3`; write `(double)7 / 2` for `3.5`. Uninitialised variables hold garbage.

exercises.title: Total weight
exercises.prompt: Write int total_kg(int bags, int kg_per_bag) that returns the total weight.

exercises.title: Exact average
exercises.prompt: Write double average(int total, int count) that returns the exact average: average(7, 2) is 3.50.

tests.hint_if_fail: 7 / 2 with ints is 3. Cast one side to double first.

hints: Both are int, so / drops the .5.

quiz.q: What is 7 / 2 in C with two ints?
Does C have a built-in string type?
choices: No: text is an array of char
quiz.why: Strings are char arrays ending in \0.
